title: Finn Star and the Lost Star Blanket
markdown:
Finn Star was the giggliest glitteriest wizard in all the Suncrumb Ridges. His hat was tall and pointy, and sometimes when he sneezed a puff of sparkly dust popped out and tickled his nose. Lumina, his moon-moth, was as small and fragile as moonlight on a quiet puddle. Her wings caught the sun in a hundred colours. She hummed like faraway chimes.

One morning sunbeams tickled him awake. His hat bounced. “Lumina!” His voice was a tiny bell. She nestled on her fluffy cloud-bed, humming a sleepy song, and something was missing. Her cozy starry blanket, usually tucked around her for dreams of dancing moonbeams and sleepy comets, was not there.

We’ll find it, Lumina. We’ll find the starry one.

He looked under the bed. Hat wobbling. Nope. Behind the toadstool chair with the mushroom cushion. Nope. Inside a boot, just in case. Silly Finn Star. A wobble in his tummy. He was a little worried about going outside when things were missing. Lumina hummed a question, feelers twitching. He patted the sparkly hat, which always made him a bit braver. “We’ll go on a grand adventure, just you and me.” A tiny happy hum, a sigh of relief. The sky was painting itself pink and orange, the hour she loved her blanket most.

So Finn Star, with Lumina fluttering like a little sparkler beside his ear, tiptoed out of the cozy cottage. The door creeeeaked open, friendly. He followed a little path that wound through the cloud-pines, the fluffiest whitest trees you ever did see, giant cotton-candy reaching up to the sky. The path smelled of warm cookies, freshly baked, and a hint of sunshine. Every step felt soft and springy, like walking on a big fluffy pillow.

They had not gone far when they heard a snooooore, then another, a rumbling bumblebee. Behind a particularly fluffy pine: a dragon no bigger than Finn Star’s boot, scales like a thousand tiny rainbows. Not a roar-grrrr dragon. A zzzzz-snuggle dragon. Flicker, the teacup dragon, stretched a little leg, yawned toasted marshmallows, and blinked honey-coloured eyes.

“Hello,” Finn Star said, shy of all that sparkle. Flicker tilted his head. “Mmmph? Blanket?” Finn giggled. Lumina fluttered. “Not yours. Lumina’s. Silver stars.” Flicker sniffed like a tiny curious puppy, puffed cinnamon smoke. “Nope! No blanket here!” He curled into a sparkly ball and napped again. “Thank you for sniffing, Flicker!”

Past more cloud-pines like scoops of ice cream, a deep rumbling chuckle, warm pebbles in a stream. On a mossy hillock like a giant green cushion sat the biggest softest ogre Finn Star had ever seen. Niamh, the cloud-sheep shepherd, smelled of sweet clover and warm sunshine. Smile as wide as a rainbow. Eyes as kind as warm puddles. She patted fluffy cloud-sheep, little balls of cotton wool bouncing on the grass.

“Good day, Niamh,” Finn Star said, braver because she was so friendly. “We’re looking for Lumina’s starry blanket. She misses it very much.”

Niamh stroked a chin as mossy as the hillock. “A starry blanket. I did see a flicker of something sparkly near the Whispering Caves. Glowy-glowy, like a tiny star fell down.”

Finn Star’s hat wiggled. Ach-choo-SPARKLE! “Thank you!” Lumina hummed a little dance. Niamh winked. “Be careful, but not too careful. It’s a gentle place.”

We’ll find it, Lumina. Glowy-glowy in the cave.

They followed Niamh’s direction toward a gentle opening in the side of a grassy hill. The cave was not dark, not spooky. Soft gentle light. Inside, glowing moss clung to the walls, a million tiny emeralds and soft green lamps. The Whispering Caves. The moss whispered tiny happy secrets as they walked past.

Finn Star took a deep breath, puffed his chest, held Lumina’s little leg. “Stay close.” He stepped inside. Moss soft and cool underfoot, tiny tinkling fairy bells. And there, tangled around a patch of the brightest glowiest moss, was Lumina’s starry blanket, silver stars sewn all over it, twinkling like tiny captured stars, a piece of the night sky come to visit.

He reached into his hat for his favourite brightest sparkle, the special shimmer that always made him feel brave. He thought about keeping it. Lumina needed her blanket. So he placed the sparkle on the softest patch of moss, a little gift for the cave, hoping it would glow even brighter. Small, and his. He untangled the blanket carefully, not pulling too hard, gentle with the pretty moss, and shook it so sparkly bits fell like tiny diamonds. It smelled of moonbeams and a hint of stardust. Fabric like stroking a whisper. The little silver stars hummed with quiet twinkly light. He held it out, heart warm.

“Here you are.”

Lumina flew down with a happy flutter, hummed with pure joy, and snuggled right into the starry blanket, a little moonbeam tucked into a starry hug. Finn Star’s hat did a happy wiggle dance. They tiptoed out, blinking in gentle sunlight, waved goodbye to the fluffy cloud-pines and still-sleeping Flicker, and skipped all the way home, the path even more like warm cookies. Back in the cottage he tucked Lumina in, blanket perfect. She hummed a sleepy lullaby. He gave her a super-duper soft hug, just because, and because the sparkle he had left in the moss was still doing its small brave job, and finding lost treasures had already been enough.
